title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. f: P -> T is a torsor under a bundle of connected topological groups U = U_T over T. Write Pi_T for the local system t -> pi_1(U_t); it is abelian because U_t is a connected group. mu (later gamma_T) is a normal, central, discrete sub-bundle of U_T. Put U_0 = U/mu and P_0 = P/mu. Then P_0 -> T is a U_0-torsor and P -> P_0 is a principal mu-covering.

Homotopy sequences. Write G = pi_1(T), G_0 = pi_1(P_0), E = pi_1(U_0) and pi = pi_1(U). Because 0 -> mu -> U -> U_0 -> 1 with mu discrete and U connected, we get 0 -> pi -> E -> mu -> 0. On the page this is written as 0 -> Pi_T -> E_T -> gamma_T -> 1. The covering P -> P_0 is classified by phi: G_0 -> mu, and phi restricted to E is the quotient map E -> mu. Then pi_1(P) = Ker phi, which sits in 1 -> pi -> Ker phi -> G -> 1. Since mu is abelian, the remark 'inc. on a pi_1ab(C_0) -> mu' says phi factors through the abelianization.

Key structural fact (bottom of page). The orbit map of a connected group action sends pi_1(U_t) into the centre of pi_1(P_x). Hence f^*(Pi_T) maps to the automorphisms of the identity functor of Pi_1 P, written 'Int Pi_1 P'. So Pi_1 P -> Pi_1 T is a Pi_T-groupoid in Grothendieck's sense: a groupoid with a functorial central action of a group (local system) on all automorphism groups.

The two statements 1°) and 2°) give the dictionary needed for the previous page's argument.
- 1°) A central E-groupoid structure C_0 on E_0 (the set of objects) gives, via C, an extension of P_{E_0} -> T as a U_0-torsor. Objects map to P_0 through the fundamental groupoid.
- 2°) Conversely, a principal mu-covering of P_0 is the same as a local system of mu-torsors on C_0 with mu acting by translations, so that C_0 = C/mu. Its monodromy pi_1(C_0, x_0) -> mu = Aut(E_{x_0}) must extend the quotient map E -> mu.

In short, the page states the topological model for: free Sigma'-groupoid C' with central mu, and quotient Sigma = Sigma'/mu with groupoid C_0 = C'/mu. It also gives the converse lifting criterion.

Purpose. The next page applies this with U_T a torus bundle with pi_1 = Z^A and gamma = mu_2^A. Then E_T is Z^A extended by mu_2^A, which is the '(Z^A, mu_2^A)-groupoid' structure of S_0T_G and its 'rigidified' quotients in the Teichmüller tower. The Z^A are Dehn twists along cut curves, central in boundary stabilizers.
errors: The sequences 1 -> pi -> Ker phi -> G -> 1 and 1 -> E -> G_0 -> G -> 1 omit the boundary map pi_2(T) -> pi_1(U_t). Left-exactness holds only if that map vanishes, e.g. T aspherical, which is true in the intended Teichmüller/moduli application but is not stated.

The sequence 0 -> Pi_T -> E_T -> gamma_T -> 1 requires gamma_T discrete (pi_0 gamma = gamma). If the parenthetical qualifier read 'connexe' it would be wrong; the application (gamma = mu_2^A) is finite, so the qualifier is probably 'commutatif'/'central'.
2°) needs C_0 connected (or a base point per component) for 'pi_1(C_0, x_0) -> mu' to classify the covering. Minor.

ideas.what: Image of pi_1 of a connected structure group lies in the centre of pi_1 of the total space, making Pi_1(P) -> Pi_1(T) a groupoid with central action of the local system Pi_T
ideas.modern_name: central action of the inertia / banded groupoid; centrality of the orbit-map image (classical H-space/transformation group fact)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (folklore, e.g. Gottlieb's work on evaluation subgroups, 1965)

ideas.what: Sigma-groupoids (groupoids with functorial central Sigma in all automorphism groups) and their quotients by a central subgroup mu: C_0 = C/mu, Sigma = Sigma'/mu
ideas.modern_name: rigidification of a stack/groupoid along a central subgroup of the inertia
ideas.usually_credited_to: Abramovich–Corti–Vistoli (2003), Romagnoli; also Giraud's banded gerbes (1971)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions Teichmüller groupoids and the role of twists, but not this formalism explicitly

ideas.what: Classification of principal mu-coverings of a quotient groupoid C_0 by local systems / homomorphisms pi_1(C_0) -> mu extending the given E -> mu
ideas.modern_name: lifting criterion for central extensions / covering theory of groupoids

ideas.what: Torus-bundle model: U_T with pi_1 = Z^A, quotient by mu_2^A giving extensions of mu_2^A by Z^A, to produce the (Z^A, mu_2^A)-groupoid structure on Teichmüller groupoids
ideas.modern_name: central Dehn-twist extensions in the Teichmüller tower; half-twists/orientation data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Schneps, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura (1990s–2000s) for the twist structure

missed.claim: Grothendieck's (Z^A, mu_2^A)-groupoid formalism for S_0T_G anticipates the rigidification of stacks along central inertia (Abramovich–Corti–Vistoli), applied to the Teichmüller tower. He works with central quotient groupoids C_0 = C/mu, modelled topologically by quotienting torsors under connected group bundles by central discrete subgroups. The pair (lattice of twists, mu_2) is treated systematically as a central 'band'.
missed.quote: Un mu-rev. principal ... défini par un système local sur C_0 ... (de façon que C_0 ≃ C/mu)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Rigidified moduli stacks and twisted-curve stacks (with mu_r-banded nodes) are now standard. The joint Z^A x mu_2^A bookkeeping of Dehn twists and their square roots could inform Grothendieck–Teichmüller lego constructions at the level of stacks rather than groups. However, the core formalism is otherwise known.

deep.surprise_reason: Technical scaffolding: a standard homotopy-sequence and central-quotient argument for groupoids, serving the Teichmüller lego of nearby pages. The only mildly interesting point is the early, systematic use of what is now called rigidification along central inertia (Z^A, mu_2^A) in the Teichmüller context.
transcription_corrections: Bottom: '0 -> Pi_T -> E_T -> gamma_T -> 1' — the parenthetical after 'U_T' looks like '(centr. comm.)' (central commutative) rather than 'central connexe'; a connected gamma would be inconsistent with the sequence.
Diagram: G_0 = pi_1(P_0) and G = pi_1(T) are labels under the terms of 1 -> E -> G_0 -> G -> 1, with phi: G_0 -> mu and the vertical E -> mu.
'f^*(Pi_T) -> Int Pi_1 P' (Int likely = automorphisms of the identity functor / interior), preceded by 'f^*(Pi_T) opère sur Pi_1 P'.
Line 3 of 1°): 'P_{E_0} -> T comme U_0-torseur'; 'E_0 -> P_0 par images des pts par groupoïde fondamental'.
'2°) Un mu-rev. principal E de P_0' — the struck word is likely 'plus'/'pt'.
